threads.body: The captured `error` is recorded on the span but never rethrown, so any exception thrown by the underlying async processor (e.g. protocol/read errors from `readMessageBegin`/`readMessageEnd`) is swallowed and never propagates to `AsyncFrameBuffer.invoke()`, which then can't transition the connection to its error/close state. This diverges from the synchronous `ServerProcessorDecorator.process` (which does `throw t;`) and from the javaagent's `ThriftTBaseAsyncProcessorInstrumentation` advice that lets the original throwable propagate — the stated goal of this PR is feature parity with that advice. Consider rethrowing while still ending the span.

This snippet declares the local as `thriftTelemetry` but then calls `telemetry.wrapServerInProtocolFactory(...)` / `telemetry.wrapServerOutProtocolFactory(...)`, referencing an undefined `telemetry` variable. Every other snippet in this README uses `thriftTelemetry`, so these two lines should use `thriftTelemetry` for the example to compile.
Grammar: "accessing a non-public members" mixes the singular article "a" with the plural "members". Since this class exposes more than one helper, drop the article.
